title: Homogeneity Poisons the Well: Synthetic-Data Distillation Amplifies Shared Errors into Model Collapse

original_idea.body:
# Homogeneity Poisons the Well: Synthetic-Data Distillation Amplifies Shared Errors into Model Collapse

**Problem:** When a new model is distilled from homogeneous teacher outputs, the shared blind spots get baked in and amplified.

**Direction:** Lightweight simulation: generate synthetic Q&A from an open small model, measure mode-coverage vs a real reference, and quantify how rare answers are dropped. Use prompt-level pseudo-distillation to show diversity loss without full retraining.

**Why it matters:** The internet is filling with homogeneous AI text; this connects today's measurable homogeneity to tomorrow's collapse, a >1-year threat.

**Relevant context:** Strong Model Collapse (ICLR 2025); distillation inheriting teacher vulnerabilities.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain to model-collapse risk, but the prompt-level pseudo-distillation proxy weakens the link to real cross-generation collapse.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference + diversity metrics via few-shot pseudo-distillation; guided, avoids full retraining.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused diversity-collapse-slope measurement; the pseudo-distillation design needs careful setup.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Long-horizon (>1yr) collapse question labs deprioritize; inference-only, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + diversity metrics, no training; low compute.

novelty.reasoning: Model collapse is studied; the homogeneity-amplifies-collapse pseudo-distillation framing may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Model collapse is studied; the homogeneity-amplifies-collapse pseudo-distillation framing may be partly open.
